children: price swings have cooled markedly, according to Grayscale Investments. The asset’s one-year realized volatility now sits at 43%—well below its decade-long average of 64% and sharply lower than the 81% recorded five years ago.
That figure places Bitcoin’s annualized volatility beneath that of 19% of S&P 500 (

) constituents. A distribution of the index’s members, drawn from Bloomberg data through October 6, 2026, shows most stocks clustered between roughly 15% and 40%, with a long right-hand tail of higher-volatility names. Bitcoin’s 43% reading falls to the right of the main peak yet remains lower than a meaningful share of large-cap equities.
The data also highlights several familiar companies for context: JPMorgan
near 70%, and more extreme outliers such as Honeywell
above 85%. Bitcoin’s measurement relies on the Bloomberg Bitcoin spot price and daily returns over the prior twelve months.

title: Bitcoin volatility is now quieter than roughly 20% of the S&P 500
